newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc falls to mid-July lows versus mark.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc falls to mid-July lows versus mark.

text.p: The Swiss franc fell to its lowest levels since mid-July against the mark in late European dealings, traders said.

One trader said the mark may have room to test 82.75 Swiss centimes, and beyond that 83.25 after it rose to 82.62 centimes on Thursday. The mark was thus at its highest levels versus the Swiss franc since 82.69 July 15.
A trader at one Swiss bank said part of the pressure reflected sales of Swiss francs for French francs.
"It (the drop in the Swiss franc) is certainly on the one hand tied to Paris/Swiss. On the other hand, we had at 82.20 relatively good support," the trader said.
Technical buying coincided with a lessening of market worries about the Russian political situation, as President Boris Yeltsin waits for a heart operation.

"One must also see that mark/Swiss came under pressure on rumours about Yeltsin, and that has calmed down," the trader added. Many participants may now be scrambling to cover short mark positions as a result, he said.
Comments by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing on Wednesday that the German central bank had no reason to further lower interest rates also supported the mark.
